Important information to read and confirm you agree and understand:

Trying for a baby

Finasteride may affect male fertility while you are taking it.
These changes are usually reversible after stopping treatment, but recovery may take several months. If you are planning to try for a baby, it is best not to use this or to stop it several months before trying to conceive.

Depression

Some people have experienced severe depression when taking finasteride. Before taking finasteride, read and keep the finasteride patient cards and patient information leaflet within your pack and inform your doctor if you have any personal history of depression or suicidal thought. You should stop taking this medication immediately if you notice that your mood is affected and speak to your doctor.

Finasteride and your prostate

Finasteride can lower the level of a prostate protein called PSA (prostate-specific antigen) in your blood. Because of this, it’s recommended that you see your GP for a prostate check (rectal examination) and a PSA blood test before starting treatment, and then at regular intervals while taking it.

How often this is needed will depend on your age and personal risk factors. These checks help to detect any prostate problems, including prostate cancer, as early as possible.

Sexual problems

If you experience decreased sex drive, difficulty having an erection or ejaculation problems on finasteride, you should contact your doctor for medical advice.

This medication is prescribed for your own personal use

If you are requesting any follow-up medication, you confirm you are tolerating your treatment and any side effects experienced.


Your answers are used to make medical decisions

Each tablet contains: finasteride 1mg


Finasteride  increases hair growth on the scalp and prevents further hair loss in men. Men with mild to moderate, but not complete hair loss, can benefit from using finasteride.

Do not take finasteride  if:
  • you are a woman (because this medicine is for men). It has been shown in clinical trials that finasteride does not work in women with hair loss.
  • you are allergic (hypersensitive) to finasteride or any of the other ingredients
  • you are already taking finasteride or dutasteride used for a prostate problem called benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).
  • you are diagnosed with depression or develop depression whilst on treatment. 

Taking this medicine
  • The usual dose is one tablet each day.
  • Take this medicine by mouth.
  • Finasteride  will not work faster or better if you take it more than once a day.

Side effects may include:
  • you may be unable to have an erection (impotence)
  • you may have less desire to have sex
  • you may have problems with ejaculation, for example a decrease in the amount of semen released during sex. This decrease in the amount of semen does not appear to affect normal sexual function.
  • you may develop mental health problems and depression. 

These side effects above may disappear after a while if you continue taking finasteride. If these symptoms persist, they usually resolve after stopping finasteride. If you develop depression, please stop immediately and speak to your doctor.

Each tablet contains: finasteride 1mg


Finasteride  increases hair growth on the scalp and prevents further hair loss in men. Men with mild to moderate, but not complete hair loss, can benefit from using finasteride.

Do not take Propecia  if:
  • you are a woman (because this medicine is for men). It has been shown in clinical trials that finasteride does not work in women with hair loss.
  • you are allergic (hypersensitive) to finasteride or any of the other ingredients
  • you are already taking finasteride or dutasteride used for a prostate problem called benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).
  • you are diagnosed with depression or develop depression whilst on treatment. 

Taking this medicine
  • The usual dose is one tablet each day.
  • Take this medicine by mouth.
  • Finasteride  will not work faster or better if you take it more than once a day.

Side effects may include:
  • you may be unable to have an erection (impotence)
  • you may have less desire to have sex
  • you may have problems with ejaculation, for example a decrease in the amount of semen released during sex. This decrease in the amount of semen does not appear to affect normal sexual function.
  • you may develop mental health problems and depression. 

These side effects above may disappear after a while if you continue taking Propecia. If these symptoms persist, they usually resolve after stopping Propecia. If you develop depression, please stop immediately and speak to your doctor.
